verses.text: Ahaz was king of Judah, the son of Jotham and grandson of Uzziah. In his day, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel, Remaliah's son, marched up to fight Jerusalem, but they couldn't take it.
Word reached David's household: “Syria has teamed up with Ephraim.” Ahaz and his people shook inside the way forest trees shake in the wind.
The LORD said to Isaiah, “Go meet Ahaz with your son Shearjashub. You'll find him at the end of the channel from the upper pool, on the road to the cloth washer's field.
Tell him, ‘Watch yourself and stay calm. Don't be scared or lose heart over these two smoking ends of burned-out torches, no matter how furious Rezin and Syria or Remaliah's son get.
Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son have made plans to hurt you. They're saying,
“Let's march up against Judah and rip it apart, split it between us, and put Tabeel's son on the throne.”
But here's what the Lord GOD says: “That plan won't stand. It won't happen.”
Damascus is the head of Syria, and Rezin is the head of Damascus. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be smashed to pieces and won't be a people anymore.
Samaria is the head of Ephraim, and Remaliah's son is the head of Samaria. If you won't believe, you won't stand firm.’”
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again.
“Ask the LORD your God for a sign. Ask for one from the depths below or the heights above.”
Ahaz said, “I won't ask. I won't put the LORD to the test.”
Isaiah said, “Listen up, family of David. Is wearing people out not enough for you? Are you going to wear out my God's patience too?
So the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the virgin will become pregnant, have a son, and name him Immanuel.
He'll eat butter and honey by the time he knows how to say no to evil and choose good.
Before the child knows how to say no to evil and choose good, the land of those two kings you can't stand will be deserted.
The LORD will bring on you, your people, and your father's household days like nothing since Ephraim broke away from Judah. He'll bring the king of Assyria.”
That day the LORD will whistle for the fly from the far ends of Egypt's rivers and for the bee from Assyria.
They'll all come and settle in the empty valleys, in the cracks in the rocks, on every thorn hedge, and in every pasture.
That day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the River, the king of Assyria, to shave the hair from head to foot and take off the beard too.
That day someone will keep a young cow and two sheep alive.
They'll give so much milk that he'll eat butter. Everyone left in the land will live on butter and honey.
That day every place that once had a thousand vines worth a thousand silver shekels will be overrun with briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows because the whole land will be covered in briers and thorns.
You won't go near the hills you used to hoe, afraid of the briers and thorns. Those hills will be places to turn oxen loose and let sheep roam.
